source.subject: Two vertically stacked soft/hard hysteresis-loop plots. No portrait, iron ring, apparatus or wire is visible.

observations: Full-resolution output: both complete panels and all eight labels are visible; no clipping, overlapping labels, blank panel or black raster failure.
The top soft-material loop retains tightly spaced near-vertical branches and a small enclosed area. The lower hard-material loop retains widely separated branches and a much larger enclosed area.

Both panels retain positive and negative saturation ends, nonzero remanence at B0=0, and nonzero opposite coercive crossings at I=0. Neither loop has an invented calibration, tick values, source-point letters or a direction annotation on its branches.
Two separate equal-scale frames preserve upward positive I and rightward positive B0 axes, nearby zero labels, and the upper-panel negative-axis terminal arrow visible in the source.
Source panel a and Cyrillic be are localized to English (a) and (b), matching both current text authorities; English soft/hard descriptors are declared modern additions.

Normal mobile-size output at 316px: both loops, all origin/axis labels and both panel descriptors remain distinct and legible. The native renderer reports 17.775px minimum final label size at this width.
No Cyrillic or Chinese output labels, portrait, old-book texture, flag, uniform, decorative Soviet symbol, equipment or wires have been introduced.
Stoletov's closed-ring method and historical identity remain bound verbatim in current lesson prose but do not license adding apparatus or a portrait to this graph source.

The contour geometry is qualitative and slightly idealized with exact opposite vertex pairs and equal panel scales. Drawing coordinates, intercepts and areas are not physical measurements or universal material constants.

The native 640px screenshot has slight subpixel seams at some polygon segment joins; these do not interrupt the contours, and the 316px image reads as continuous. This does not defeat the instructional comparison and is not grounds for an additional polishing render.
